source.quoted_text: Central Sch. I Art. 62: 'TRANSFER (whether with or without consideration) — (a) of shares in an incorporated company or other body corporate — [Twenty-five paise] for hundred rupees or part thereof of the value of the share' = 0.25%. Rounding proviso (same 2004 order): duty 'shall, wherever necessary, be rounded off to the next five paise'. NOTE: transfer of SHARES is Union law — the Maharashtra Schedule I has NO share-transfer entry (Art 59 'Transfer' covers only debentures, interest secured by bond/mortgage/policy, Administrator-General property and trust property). This pre-amendment regime governs transfers executed BEFORE 1 July 2020.

source.quoted_text: Founder ruling (Q4, 2026-07-16): 'Physical share transfers on Form SH-4 attract stamp duty at 0.015% of consideration under Article 62 of the Indian Stamp Act as amended, uniform across India — effective 1 July 2020 ... NO STATE DEVIATION IS PERMITTED; documents still citing 0.25% are outdated.' Per the DEA FAQs, off-market transfers WITHOUT consideration (gifts) attract nil duty, the base being consideration. Corroborated structurally: the Maharashtra Schedule has no competing share-transfer entry.
